t: Post-2000 Poetry: Poems of the Decade

shakespeare-tragedy-or-comedy: Othello, Lear, Hamlet: is the flaw in the hero or the world?
other-drama-pre-or-post-1900: Why do audiences pay to watch a good person destroyed?
prose-theme-crime-and-detection: Every crime story asks 'whodunit'. What else is it asking?
prose-theme-science-and-society: Frankenstein and the Martians: what do writers fear science will do?
prose-theme-the-supernatural: Why does the Gothic keep returning to locked rooms and family secrets?
prose-theme-women-and-society: How do novels show women's lives when the law gave them few rights?
post-2000-poetry-poems-of-the-decade: A poem from this century, no critics yet: how do you write about it?
unseen-poetry-comparison: What does A-level want from an unseen poem that GCSE didn't?
othello: Shakespeare's source took months. Why squeeze it into two days?
king-lear: Why does King Lear tell the same story twice?
hamlet: Revenge plays had a recipe. Does Hamlet follow it or rewrite it?
tess-of-the-durbervilles: Hardy cuts Tess's life into seven 'Phases'. Why not just chapters?
frankenstein: Three narrators, one monster. Whose story can we trust?
dracula: Journals, letters, cuttings: why does Dracula never get a diary?
wuthering-heights: Why do a stranger and a servant tell this great love story?
